- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 82), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above true peak or adjust downward by 2–3 points if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates downward trend — add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend — if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3 points within first 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/– values).
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat or declining, model overreacts — reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid over-optimism.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to average out — use median of recent 5-day trend instead of 30-day forecast for better alignment.
